Purpose: Portable source-bound independent review admission for Windows system-event inert tests.

SourceFiles.FullFileReviewScope: Event export only; other existing exports are bound for drift, not independently qualified here.

Normalization: Strict UTF8 text decoding removes a leading UTF8 BOM when present; CRLF and lone CR normalize to LF for comparison/body hashing. Raw hashes bind actual canonical bytes; raw copies differing in line endings or BOM are not claimed identical.
ValidityPolicy: Before treating a row as reviewed, verify every SourceFiles raw/full and normalized-LF hash, exact selector set/count, normalized body hash, and adjacent four rationale comments. Any mismatch makes affected admission UNREVIEWED; conservatively invalidate all rows on any bound source change. An artifact does not execute or enforce this policy by itself.

PublicRecordedExecution.Scope: Canonical 14 inert mocked public event contracts; no real Event Log or DLL query
Selectors: maps every public field from real-shape synthetic XML values
passes the requested window and count above the former hardcap
accepts a successful empty native array without fallback
falls back when native fails with NULL
falls back on native exceptions without declaring a quiet machine
falls back on malformed native JSON
rejects the old fabricated native shape
rejects a top-level object instead of the array contract
rejects bad fields without publishing an earlier valid partial row
rejects inconsistent severity and invalid timestamp fields
bypasses the two-argument native ABI for IncludeInfo
holds real fallback failures instead of returning empty success
allows only the benign no-events fallback to return empty
preserves CRLF first-line and full-message equality across native and fallback

EvidencePortability: All consumer source/fixture bindings are repository-relative. Embedded review/execution summaries and hashes are provenance; no private evidence path is required to check current source validity.
RemainingGaps: Windows target compile/lint and nineteen inert Rust test execution
Real Event Log, publisher formatting/localization, real DLL and cross-language ABI runtime
No performance benchmark or total process-memory cap proof
Allocation failure is not universally recoverable; release panic=abort still aborts
A synchronous Windows API may overrun its admission budget
Combined severity/timestamp rejection does not independently prove each public check
